[maas-code-reviewer review]

> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


The sentinel design matches the established BIND9 hardening-option convention (dns_fetches_per_zone/server use the same `value or (default if hardening else 0)` pattern), and both nginx templates already gate limit_req/limit_conn on a non-empty `api_rate_limit_rate`, so limiting is genuinely off by default on unhardened deployments. Tests cover both services, including real-template rendering on the region side. Three issues to address before merge: (1) an explicit 0 is now accepted by the relaxed validators (min changed 1 -> 0) but silently rewritten to the default by the `or 60` / `or 100` fallbacks, so `api_rate_limit_burst: 0` can never take effect, contradicting the commit description's claim that a burst of 0 stays configurable; (2) the rack-side options are validated with formencode `Number`, which accepts fractional values, not `Int` as the commit description claims, so e.g. `api_conn_limit: 2.5` renders an invalid `limit_conn api_conn 2.5;` into rackd.nginx.conf; (3) the doc statement that leaving `api_rate_limit_rate` empty turns off limiting is no longer true when hardening is active — hardened deployments that had explicitly emptied it to disable throttling get silently re-enabled at 20r/s after this change, which the docs should call out.

docs/reference/configuration-guides/secu.264: 'leaving it empty turns off both rate and connection limiting' is no longer unconditionally true: when hardening is active, an empty `api_rate_limit_rate` falls back to 20r/s (plus burst 60 / conn 100), so a hardened deployment has no way to disable limiting at all. The previous text promised unconditional off, meaning hardened setups that set it empty to disable throttling will be silently re-throttled at 20r/s after this change. Consider qualifying the sentence, e.g. 'when hardening is not active, leaving it empty turns off both rate and connection limiting; when hardening is active, the defaults above always apply'.

src/maasserver/config.py.335: Relaxing min from 1 to 0 makes 0 valid input, but the consumer silently coerces it back (`api_rate_limit_burst or 60`, `api_conn_limit or 100` in regiondservices/http.py), and `if_missing=0` makes an unset key indistinguishable from an explicit 0 — so `api_rate_limit_burst: 0` is accepted yet always renders as burst=60. The commit description claims 'a burst of 0 (reject excess requests instead of queueing them) stays configurable', which this cannot deliver. Either keep min=1 so 0 is rejected loudly (as before), or use a real unset sentinel (e.g. if_missing=None plus a None check) so an explicit 0 can reach the template.

src/maasserver/regiondservices/http.py.140: `or 60` here (and `or 100` for api_conn_limit on the next line) also catches an explicitly configured 0, silently rendering burst=60 / conn=100. nginx's own default burst of 0 (reject excess requests immediately instead of queueing them) is therefore unreachable, contradicting the commit description. If 0 should be settable, distinguish it from 'unset' (e.g. a None-based sentinel in RegionConfiguration) rather than relying on falsiness.

src/provisioningserver/config.py.902: Unlike maasserver/config.py, which validates these same options with formencode `Int`, `Number` converts 'to a float or integer' (Number(min=0).to_python('2.5') == 2.5), so a fractional `api_rate_limit_burst` — and `api_conn_limit` on line 908 — in rackd.conf passes validation and renders `burst=2.5` into rackd.nginx.conf, which nginx will not accept. The commit description states 'both are validated with Int so a fractional value cannot reach the NGINX config'; use Int(min=0, if_missing=0) here to make that true (cf. maasserver/dns/config.py:126, which defensively wraps Number results with int()).

src/provisioningserver/rackdservices/htt.255: Same issue as the region side: `api_rate_limit_burst or 60` and `api_conn_limit or 100` silently replace an explicit 0 in rackd.conf with 60/100, so burst=0 / conn=0 can never be configured even though ClusterConfiguration now accepts 0 (min relaxed from 1 to 0). If 0 is meant to remain a real value, distinguish it from 'unset' (e.g. if_missing=None) instead of relying on falsiness.
